title: Vagus Nerve Collection and Histology for Microscopy
author: J. Ashley Ezzell
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bh4bj8sn
materials: We rinsed each sample with deionized water.
We rinsed the slides in distilled water.

steps.title: Perfuse Rats
steps.instruction: Perfuse Sprague-Dawley rats with phosphate buffered saline and paraformaldehyde.

substeps.instruction: Perfuse with ~300 mL phosphate buffered saline (or until the liver is cleared).
Perfuse with ~300 mL 4% paraformaldehyde (or until joints and tissues are stiff).

steps.title: Collect Vagus Nerve Samples
steps.instruction: Harvest the carotid sheath and esophagus samples.

substeps.instruction: Collect bilateral samples of the carotid sheath in the neck from the clavicle up to where the nerve and carotid intermingle with non-parallel nerves.
Measure from the 'valley' of the common carotid bifurcation to the center of each sample.
Collect the esophagus from the diaphragm to the stomach with the subdiaphragmatic vagus nerves attached.

steps.title: Prepare Samples for Processing
steps.instruction: Mark and store samples in fixative.

substeps.instruction: Dye the rostral end of each sample green to maintain orientation.
Place each sample between two histology sponges in a mega-sized histology cassette.
Store cassettes in a tub with 4% paraformaldehyde in a 4°C refrigerator.

steps.title: Tissue Processing
steps.instruction: Process samples using a Leica ASP300S Tissue Processor on the long cycle for ~10 hours.

substeps.instruction: Clearite: 50 min, three times.
Paraffin wax: 50 min, three times.

steps.title: Embedding and Sectioning
steps.instruction: Embed samples and collect transverse sections.

substeps.instruction: Embed each sample in a paraffin block oriented for transverse sections.
Trim to the center of the sample.
Collect 5 µm sections, placing two serial sections per slide for fifteen slides.

steps.title: Slide Drying and Baking
steps.instruction: Dry and bake the collected slides.

substeps.instruction: Air dry slides overnight at room temperature.
Bake slides at 37°C overnight.

steps.title: Masson's Trichrome Staining
steps.instruction: Stain slides 2 and 14 of the 15 slides per sample using Masson's trichrome.

substeps.instruction: Bake slides at 60°C for 1.5 hours, then cool overnight.
Deparaffinize and hydrate to distilled water: xylene (2x 6 min), 100% ethanol (5 min), 95% ethanol (4 min), 70% ethanol (3 min), dH2O (2x 1 min).
Place slides in Bouin's fixative (mordant) at room temperature overnight.
Wash in running tap water until yellow color disappears (~10 minutes).
Place in Weigert's Iron Hematoxylin solution for 10 min.
Wash in running tap water for 10 min.
Place in Biebrich Scarlet-Acid Fuchsin solution for 5 min.
Wash in running tap water for 2 min.
Place in Phosphomolybdic-Phosphotungstic Acid solution for 10 min.
Transfer directly to Aniline Blue solution for 3 min.
Differentiate counterstain (A. blue) in 1% Acetic Acid solution for 1 min.
Dehydrate, clear, and coverslip: 95% ethanol (1 min), 100% ethanol (4 min), xylene (5 min).

steps.title: Imaging
steps.instruction: Image the samples using a Nikon Ti2 microscope with a Photometrics Prime 95B-25MM camera.

substeps.instruction: Image at 20x magnification.
Select the best of four slices per sample based on quality (no tearing or fraying).
